title: Linear Versus Logarithmic Scale
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Plot the same eight earthquakes on a linear axis and then a logarithmic one. Nothing about the data changes; only the axis does.

learningObjectives: Compare the same dataset on linear and logarithmic axes.
Explain why a logarithmic scale is necessary when values span many orders of magnitude.

keyQuestions: Why do seven bars vanish on the linear axis when none of them is zero?
What does one equal step up the logarithmic axis represent?
When would a linear axis be the honest choice instead?
commonMisconceptions: Reading a log axis as if equal heights meant equal differences.
Believing a magnitude 8 earthquake is "twice as bad" as a magnitude 4.
Treating a bar that looks like zero as a measurement of zero.
assessmentOpportunities: States why the linear view is misleading without calling it wrong.
Explains equal spacing on a log axis as equal *ratios*, not equal differences.
Names a second quantity from this book that would need a log axis.
